content:
incident-bot: PAGER — SEV-1: GPU serving pool saturation detected in us-west-2. 429s reported for multiple customers on high-throughput routes (models: redwood-13b-v1, opt-6.7b). Paging @oncall-sre and @infra. Full alert: average queue depth > 1200 reqs, per-GPU util 98%.

sre-jen: I'm on the page. seeing sustained queue growth from hotpath; autoscaler attempted but hit an autoscale lock. logs are noisy with 'scale_lock_acquire_timeout'.

infra-sam: grabbing autoscaler logs now. initial look: lock held by 'backfill' job, backfill stuck in WAITING for 14m. also seeing token-bucket rejects at the gateway: many 429s stamped with ratepolicy=tiered-low.

ml-raf: from model side: p99 latency spiking to 12s, and token consumption per request increased due to longer context for some prod customers. token window estimates exceed normal.

oncall-sre: Acknowledge. stepping in as primary. first priority: stop customer-facing 429s. second: ensure autoscaler can actually scale.

ops-lucy: Quick mitigation options: 1) temporarily relax token-bucket thresholds for affected tiers; 2) enable burstpool routing for hot requests; 3) manually increase pool max size. We should pick a safe short-term combo.

sre-jen: I'm +1 to (1) and (3). relaxing token-bucket for low/medium tiers to reduce 429s will let traffic through while we fix autoscaler lock.

infra-sam: Executing manual pool increase first. CLI: 
```bash
redwood infra pool update --region us-west-2 --pool gpu-hotpath --max-instances 40 --reason "emergency capacity bump"
```
Applying now. ETA ~ 90s for new nodes to join.

deploy-bot: deploy queued — pool config change rolled out to infra control plane (change-id: d2f3b9).

sre-jen: Observing new nodes joining. queue depth dropping slightly. still seeing bursts of 429s from the gateway though — token checks still rejecting.

ops-lucy: I'll do a temporary token-bucket tune for the affected tier. command: 
```yaml
api: update-ratepolicy --name tiered-low --token_rate 2500 --burst 800 --duration 10m --note "emergency relax to mitigate 429s"
```
Applying now.

infra-sam: ratepolicy updated. token_rate bumped, burst allowed. gateway sync confirmed.

support-maya: Support note: customers A, B, C reported increased 429s starting ~14:12 UTC. I'll notify them of active mitigation and expected state in 15m. drafting message now. :raised_hands:

pm-alex: tagging PMs and SRE leads. we need an incident timeline + customer impact writeup after stabilization. please capture which customers hit and for how long.

ml-raf: Monitoring: 429 rate fell 70% within 120s of the ratepolicy change. CPU/GPU queue depth trending down from peak 1240 -> 420 in the last 3m. p99 latency down to ~3.5s.

sre-jen: Good. Now to address root autoscaler lock. infra-sam, what's the lock owner?

infra-sam: Lock owner is orchestration job id backfill-2026-03-15-1410 stuck in WAITING due to driver pod failing to ack. I'm force-releasing the lock to allow autoscaler to proceed. 

infra-sam: Running: 
```bash
redwood autoscale lock release --id backfill-2026-03-15-1410 --force --by ops-lucy
```
Lock released. Triggering scale check.

sre-jen: Autoscaler performed scale-up pass and provisioned 6 additional GPU nodes. new pool size reached 38. Observed request queue processing catch-up.

oncall-sre: Nice. Next: schedule a brief rollback window for the tokenpolicy change (10m). If stable, we'll keep it but need to log the config drift for audit.

ops-lucy: Set to auto-revert in 10m unless we extend. also creating a short-lived route to burstpool for top-traffic customers (manual route override).

support-maya: Customer update sent: "We're mitigating a capacity issue impacting some requests; we're applying short-term configuration changes and scaling capacity. No data was exposed. We'll provide another update in 30 minutes."

pm-alex: Can we confirm no degraded correctness for outputs? any regression after tokenpolicy relax?

ml-raf: Spot-checked top 5 flows; no regressions observed. token-bucket only governs admission not model behavior. watch eval hooks for noisy outputs though.

sre-jen: Monitoring 5m. 429s returned to baseline, queue depth under 200, latency stable. marking active mitigation success.

infra-sam: Note: the real root cause seems to be twofold: an orchestration backfill job deadlock (prevented autoscale) + aggressive tiered tokenbucket config that prevented fallback routing when pool saturated. We'll need follow-ups: remove single-point lock during backfill, adjust tier policies to allow emergency overflow to burstpool, and add better guardrails on token_rate vs expected token window.

oncall-sre: Handoff to next on-call: @oncall-sre (ops-lucy) will be primary; summary: emergency capacity bump to 38 nodes; tokenpolicy relaxed for 10m then auto-reverted; autoscaler lock force-released; 429s reduced to baseline; customers notified. Escalation level: postmortem required.

ops-lucy: Acknowledge handoff. I'll stay on for 30m to monitor and collect logs for postmortem.

sre-jen: Adding immediate follow-ups: 
- ticket INC-2026-03-15-001: investigate autoscaler lock root cause and add timeout/alert.
- ticket CFG-2026-03-15-002: review tokenbucket defaults and implement emergency-overflow policy to burstpool when hotpath saturation detected.
- runbook update: add steps to safely bump pool max and tokenpolicy relax commands.

support-maya: Logging customer impact details to incident record. so far ~4 customers experienced degraded throughput for ~18m window. will attach request IDs.

pm-alex: Good. Please add timeline and postmortem owner. assigning to @sre-jen.

deploy-bot: control-plane config change (d2f3b9) audited. Reversion schedule: 10m from now unless manually extended by ops-lucy.

sre-jen: Thanks everyone. I'll kick off the postmortem draft after wrap. closing active mitigation. :white_check_mark:

infra-sam: Dumping logs for retention: s3://redwood-incidents/2777777777/ (autoscaler, gateway, backfill).

ops-lucy: leaving a final note for next oncall: if you see this pattern again, do not try gradual token_policy reductions — prefer the emergency overflow routing + scale bump combination.

support-maya: Closing customer comms on this thread. will follow up with detailed Affected Customer list.

oncall-sre: Handoff complete. moving to monitoring channel.

sre-jen: last check: all green. incident status -> "mitigated". will publish postmortem in #postmortems within 48h.
